archetypes.name: git-porcelain
archetypes.rationale: Volatile run-log cleanup now drives git reset/restore/clean and must not leave dirty state or drop substantive logs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the run-log volatile-only classification and cleanup path in python/run_logs.py. Check whether porcelain parsing, untracked directory handling, staged changes, scrubbed files, and repo-wide cleanliness assertions behave safely for real git status output. Verify canonical token/timing artifacts cannot be skipped as volatile sidecars. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: gh-create
archetypes.rationale: PR creation no longer parses JSON and now recovers via list/view/URL fallbacks with branch and repo validation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the gh.pr_create recovery flow after removing unsupported gh pr create --json usage. Check fresh-create success, conflict recovery, stdout versus stderr URL handling, repo/branch validation, lagging pr list, and current-branch pr view fallback behavior. Look for cases where a wrong PR could be accepted or a valid created PR could be missed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: merge-race
archetypes.rationale: The merge path now polls PR head OID after force-push recovery and may reroute to CI_NOT_READY.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the merge force-push recovery and post-push OID polling changes in python/merge.py. Check whether lagged GitHub state, UNKNOWN mergeStateStatus retries, CI_NOT_READY reruns, and exhausted mismatch paths preserve the intended bash parity and avoid merging stale heads. Pay special attention to state comparisons before and after _ensure_head_matches_pr returns. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stdio-quiet
archetypes.rationale: Python ship and CI breadcrumbs were added while stdout must remain a single JSON object for the orchestrator.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate stdout and stderr behavior across python/ship.py, python/ci_monitor.py, and python/logging_util.py. Confirm breadcrumbs cannot pollute stdout, quiet-mode routing honors the expected file descriptor and log-file contracts, and unexpected exceptions still preserve machine-readable stdout. Look for environment combinations where messages are lost, duplicated, or routed to a closed descriptor. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: py311-floor
archetypes.rationale: The runtime floor is lowered to Python 3.11 across docs, guards, linters, and CI, so drift or 3.12-only syntax would break consumers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the Python 3.11 floor changes across packaging, lint/type configuration, CI matrix, shell guards, and documentation. Check for remaining runtime 3.12 assumptions or syntax/features that would fail under Python 3.11 despite the lowered requires-python and guards. Also verify contributor-tooling 3.12 requirements remain distinct from runtime requirements. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
